text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthYour Immune System Ages in Two Big BurstsYour 40s and 60s are periods of intense remodelingJCBy Jake Currie3:30 PM CDT on October 2, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleObviously our bodies change a lot as we age, and culturally we tend to focus on the ones we can see—wrinkles, weight gain, loss of muscle mass, etc. But the most dramatic alterations may be happening beneath the surface. The immune system, for example, undergoes quite a bit of remodeling as we get older. What’s going beneath the surface of that system, though?To find out, a team of researchers led by immunologists from Duke University drilled down to the cellular level. They investigated the genetic activity of 3.8 million immune cells from close to 2,000 healthy people between the ages of 19 and 97 in Singapore, and recently published their findings in Nature Communications. Read more: “Watch Immune System Cells Gobble Up Cancer Cells”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
